people.name: Simeon
people.description: Grandfather of the priest Mattathias of Modin; named only in his genealogy.

people.name: John
people.description: Father of the priest Mattathias of Modin.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Mattathias' son John Gaddis, Simon's son John (Hyrcanus) and John father of Eupolemus.

people.name: Mattathias
people.description: Priest of the course of Joarib living at Modin who killed an apostate and a royal officer and began the revolt; died in year 146 and was buried at Modin.
people.descent_note: 'Of the sons of Joarib' (2:1; 14:29) names his priestly course/ancestral house (Jehoiarib), not his father.

people.name: mother of Simon (wife of Mattathias)
people.description: Mother of Simon (and wife of Mattathias), for whom Simon set up one of the seven pyramids at Modin.
people.identity_note: Only 'his mother' in Simon's monument; that she was Mattathias' wife is inferred from 'his father, his mother' in the same verse. Not explicitly said to be mother of all five brothers.

people.name: John
people.description: Eldest son of Mattathias, surnamed Gaddis; seized and (by implication) killed by the sons of Jambri from Medaba while escorting baggage to the Nabataeans.
people.identity_note: 9:35 'his brother' and 9:38/9:42 'John their brother' identify him with John Gaddis. His death is implied by 9:42 ('avenged the blood of their brother'), not narrated explicitly.

people.name: Simon
people.description: Son of Mattathias called Thassi; succeeded Jonathan as leader, became high priest and ethnarch, took the Jerusalem citadel, and was murdered at Dok near Jericho by his son-in-law Ptolemy son of Abubus.

people.name: Judas
people.description: Third son of Mattathias, called Maccabaeus; military leader of the revolt who rededicated the temple, defeated Nicanor, sought a Roman alliance, and fell in battle against Bacchides at Elasa.

people.name: Eleazar
people.description: Son of Mattathias called Avaran; killed when the war elephant he stabbed at Beth-zechariah fell on him.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Eleazar father of the envoy Jason (8:17).

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: Youngest son of Mattathias called Apphus; succeeded Judas, was made high priest by Alexander Balas, was seized by Trypho at Ptolemais and killed at Bascama; buried at Modin.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Jonathan son of Saul (4:30) and Jonathan son of Absalom (13:11). 13:16-19 mentions two of his sons sent as hostages (unnamed group, not entered).

people.name: John
people.description: Son of Simon, made commander of the forces at Gazara; defeated Cendebaeus, escaped Ptolemy son of Abubus' plot, and succeeded his father as high priest.
people.identity_note: Known historically as John Hyrcanus I; the surname does not occur in the WEB text of 1 Maccabees. Distinct from John Gaddis, his uncle.

people.name: Judas
people.description: Son of Simon who fought beside his brother John against Cendebaeus and was wounded; murdered with his father at Dok.
people.identity_note: Distinct from his uncle Judas Maccabaeus and Judas son of Chalphi.

people.name: Mattathias
people.description: Son of Simon, murdered with his father and brother at the banquet in Dok near Jericho.
people.identity_note: Distinct from his grandfather Mattathias and from Mattathias son of Absalom.

people.name: daughter of Simon (wife of Ptolemy son of Abubus)
people.description: Simon's daughter, implied by the statement that Ptolemy son of Abubus was the high priest's son-in-law.
people.identity_note: Not mentioned directly; inferred only from 'son-in-law' in 16:12.

people.name: Philip
people.description: Father of Alexander the Macedonian (Philip II of Macedon).
people.identity_note: Distinct from Philip king of Chittim defeated by Rome (8:5, Philip V) and Philip the friend of Antiochus IV (6:14).

people.name: Alexander
people.description: Alexander the Macedonian, son of Philip, who defeated Darius, ruled over Greece and the east, divided his kingdom among his servants, and died after reigning twelve years.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Alexander Epiphanes (Balas) of chapters 10-11.

people.name: Darius
people.description: King of the Persians and Medes defeated by Alexander (Darius III).
people.identity_note: Not the Darius of Ezra/Haggai or Daniel; new person.

people.name: Antiochus
aliases: Antiochus the great king of Asia
people.description: Seleucid king, father of Antiochus Epiphanes; 'the great king of Asia' who was defeated and captured by the Romans and made tributary.
people.identity_note: 1:10 'Antiochus the king' (father of Epiphanes) and 8:6 'Antiochus the great king of Asia' are both Antiochus III the Great; merged on historical grounds.

people.name: Seleucus
people.description: Father of Demetrius I (Seleucus IV Philopator).

people.name: Antiochus Epiphanes
people.description: Seleucid king, son of Antiochus, formerly a hostage at Rome; invaded Egypt, plundered the temple and enforced the apostasy; died in Persia in year 149.
people.identity_note: Also referred to as 'the king' throughout chapters 1-6 (only key verses listed). 6:23 'your father' (addressing Antiochus V) and 10:1 (father of Alexander Epiphanes) included.

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: Son of Antiochus Epiphanes, raised by Lysias and crowned as Eupator; besieged the sanctuary, then was killed with Lysias by the army when Demetrius took the throne.

people.name: Lysias
people.description: Nobleman of royal lineage left in charge of the kingdom and of young Antiochus; campaigned against Judas and became regent for Eupator; killed by the army under Demetrius.

people.name: Philip
people.description: One of Antiochus Epiphanes' friends, appointed over the kingdom and guardian of his son; returned to seize Antioch and was defeated there by Lysias and the king.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Philip II (father of Alexander) and Philip V (8:5). His fate after 6:63 is not stated.

people.name: Demetrius
people.description: Son of Seleucus who came from Rome and took the throne in year 151, sent Bacchides, Alcimus and Nicanor against Judea, and fell in battle against Alexander Epiphanes.
people.identity_note: Distinct from his son Demetrius II (from 10:67 on). 15:1 names him as father of Antiochus VII.

people.name: Alexander Epiphanes
people.description: Claimant styled son of Antiochus who seized Ptolemais in year 160, defeated Demetrius I, married Cleopatra daughter of Ptolemy, made Jonathan high priest, and was beheaded in Arabia by Zabdiel.
people.identity_note: Historically Alexander Balas; the text calls him 'son of Antiochus' (10:1), a claim historians doubt. Distinct from Alexander the Great.

people.name: Demetrius
people.description: Son of Demetrius I who came from Crete in year 165, became king in year 167 after Ptolemy's intervention, alienated Jonathan, later recognised Simon, and was captured by Arsaces in Media.
people.identity_note: Distinct from his father Demetrius I. 'Demetrius' princes' (11:63; 12:24) included.

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: Young child of Alexander Epiphanes raised by Imalcue the Arabian, set on the throne by Trypho, and later treacherously killed by him.

people.name: Tryphon
people.description: Former partisan of Alexander who championed the boy Antiochus, captured and killed Jonathan, murdered Antiochus VI and reigned in his place, and was besieged at Dor by Antiochus VII before fleeing to Orthosia.

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: Son of Demetrius who wrote to Simon granting privileges, returned in year 174, besieged Trypho at Dor, then broke with Simon and sent Cendebaeus against Judea.
people.identity_note: Historically Antiochus VII Sidetes, son of Demetrius I. 16:18 'the king' to whom Ptolemy son of Abubus wrote is presumably also he but is not listed.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.description: King of Egypt defeated by Antiochus Epiphanes; later gave his daughter Cleopatra to Alexander, then to Demetrius II, took Antioch and the crown of Asia, and died three days after Alexander's death.
people.identity_note: 1:18 and 10:51-11:18 are both Ptolemy VI Philometor historically (reigned c. 180-145 BC); merged. Distinct from the King Ptolemy addressed by Lucius (15:16) and from Ptolemy son of Dorymenes / son of Abubus.

people.name: Cleopatra
people.description: Daughter of King Ptolemy, married to Alexander Epiphanes at Ptolemais and then given by her father to Demetrius II.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.description: King of Egypt to whom the Roman consul Lucius addressed his letter on behalf of the Jews.
people.identity_note: Historically Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II (c. 139 BC); distinct from Ptolemy VI who died at 11:18.

people.name: Dorymenes
people.description: Father of Ptolemy, one of the generals chosen by Lysias.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.description: Son of Dorymenes, one of the king's friends chosen by Lysias with Nicanor and Gorgias to invade Judea.

people.name: Abubus
people.description: Father of Ptolemy the governor of the plain of Jericho.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.description: Governor of the plain of Jericho and son-in-law of Simon, who murdered Simon and two of his sons at a banquet in Dok and tried to kill John.

spouses.ref_name: daughter of Simon (wife of Ptolemy son of Abubus)

people.name: chief collector of tribute
people.description: Royal tax official sent by Antiochus IV two years after the temple plunder, who attacked Jerusalem treacherously.
people.identity_note: Unnamed in 1 Maccabees; 2 Maccabees 5:24 names an Apollonius for a similar mission, but no merge is made here.

people.name: Jew who sacrificed at Modin
people.description: Jew who came forward to sacrifice on the pagan altar at Modin and was killed by Mattathias.

people.name: king's officer at Modin
people.description: Royal officer compelling sacrifice at Modin, killed by Mattathias.

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: Commander who led Gentile forces from Samaria against Israel and was killed by Judas, who took his sword.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Apollonius governor of Coelesyria under Demetrius II (10:69-79), about 20 years later.

people.name: Seron
people.description: Commander of the army of Syria defeated by Judas at the ascent of Beth-horon.

people.name: Nicanor
people.description: One of the king's friends sent against Judea; later sent by Demetrius I, threatened the temple, and fell at Adasa on 13 Adar, where his head and hand were displayed.
people.identity_note: 3:38 (under Lysias) and 7:26 (under Demetrius I) are taken as the same man, as is usual; the text does not state it explicitly.

people.name: Gorgias
people.description: One of the king's friends; led the night raid against Judas near Emmaus and later defeated Joseph and Azarias at Jamnia.

people.name: Bacchides
people.description: Friend of Demetrius I and ruler beyond the river who installed Alcimus, defeated and killed Judas at Elasa, fortified Judea, and finally made peace with Jonathan.

people.name: Alcimus
people.description: Leader of the Hellenizing party made high priest by Demetrius I; a priest of Aaron's line who killed sixty Hasidaeans and died of a paralytic stroke while demolishing the inner court wall.
people.identity_note: 7:14 calls him 'a priest of the seed of Aaron'.

people.name: Timotheus
people.description: Leader of the Ammonite force and of the Gentile army in Gilead, defeated by Judas.
people.identity_note: 5:6 (Ammon) and 5:11-40 (Gilead) are treated as one man; 1 Maccabees has no other Timothy. Possible distinctions from the Timothy/Timotheus figures of 2 Maccabees are left for cross-book review.

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: Governor of Coelesyria for Demetrius II who challenged Jonathan and was defeated near Azotus.
people.identity_note: Distinct from the Apollonius killed by Judas in 3:11.

people.name: Lasthenes
people.description: Official addressed by Demetrius II as 'kinsman' and 'father' in the letter confirming Jewish privileges.
people.identity_note: 'Father' in 11:32 is a court honorific, not kinship; no parent link made.

people.name: Athenobius
people.description: Friend of Antiochus VII sent to Jerusalem to demand Joppa, Gazara and the citadel from Simon.

people.name: Cendebaeus
people.description: Commander of the sea coast for Antiochus VII who fortified Kidron and raided Judea; routed by John and Judas son of Simon.

people.name: Zabdiel
people.description: Arabian who beheaded the fugitive Alexander and sent his head to Ptolemy.

people.name: Imalcue
people.description: Arabian who was raising Alexander's young son Antiochus.

people.name: Odomera
people.description: Leader struck down with his kindred by Jonathan during Bacchides' siege of Bethbasi.

people.name: Zacharias
people.description: Father of Joseph, one of the commanders left in Judea.

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Son of Zacharias, left with Azarias to guard Judea; disobeyed orders, attacked Jamnia and was defeated by Gorgias.
people.identity_note: Distinct from the patriarch Joseph (2:53).

people.name: Azarias
people.description: Commander left with Joseph son of Zacharias in Judea, defeated at Jamnia.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Azariah companion of Daniel (2:59).

people.name: Accos
people.description: Grandfather of the envoy Eupolemus.
people.identity_note: Possibly of the priestly house of Hakkoz (Ezra 2:61), but not mapped.

people.name: John
people.description: Son of Accos and father of the envoy Eupolemus.

people.name: Eupolemus
people.description: Envoy chosen by Judas and sent to Rome to establish friendship and alliance.

people.name: Eleazar
people.description: Father of the envoy Jason.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Eleazar Avaran.

people.name: Jason
people.description: Envoy sent by Judas to Rome with Eupolemus.
people.identity_note: Possibly the father of the envoy Antipater (12:16), but the text does not say so; kept separate.

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: Father of the envoy Numenius.
people.identity_note: A Jew, not one of the Seleucid kings.

people.name: Numenius
people.description: Envoy sent by Jonathan to Rome and Sparta, later by Simon to Rome with a gold shield.

people.name: Jason
people.description: Father of the envoy Antipater.
people.identity_note: Possibly identical with Jason son of Eleazar (8:17); not merged.

people.name: Antipater
people.description: Envoy sent with Numenius to Rome and Sparta.

people.name: Absalom
people.description: Father of Mattathias and of Jonathan, officers under the Hasmoneans.
people.identity_note: 11:70 and 13:11 both say 'son of Absalom'; treated as the same father (so the two officers would be brothers), but the text does not confirm this. Not King David's son.

people.name: Mattathias
people.description: Captain who stood firm with Jonathan at the battle of Hazor.

people.name: Chalphi
people.description: Father of Judas, one of Jonathan's captains.

people.name: Judas
people.description: Captain who stood firm with Jonathan at the battle of Hazor.

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: Commander sent by Simon with an army to take Joppa.

people.name: Onias
people.description: Earlier high priest who received a letter of kinship from Arius king of the Spartans.
people.identity_note: Historically Onias I (c. 300 BC) if Arius is Areus I; some identify Onias III. Kept as one person.

people.name: Arius
people.description: King of the Spartans who wrote to the high priest Onias claiming kinship with the Jews.
people.identity_note: Historically Areus I of Sparta (309-265 BC).

people.name: Philip
people.description: Macedonian king defeated by the Romans (Philip V).

people.name: Perseus
people.description: King of Chittim (Macedonia) defeated by the Romans.

people.name: Eumenes
people.description: King who received territories taken by Rome from Antiochus (Eumenes II of Pergamum).

people.name: Arsaces
people.description: King of Persia and Media who captured Demetrius II.
people.identity_note: Dynastic name of the Parthian kings; historically Mithridates I.

people.name: prince of Arsaces
people.description: One of Arsaces' princes, sent to capture Demetrius II alive.

people.name: Lucius
people.description: Consul of the Romans who wrote to kings and states in favour of the Jews.
people.identity_note: Historically probably Lucius Caecilius Metellus or Lucius Calpurnius Piso (c. 139 BC).

people.name: Attalus
people.description: King (Attalus II of Pergamum) to whom the Roman letter was also sent.

people.name: Arathes
people.description: King (Ariarathes V of Cappadocia) to whom the Roman letter was also sent.

people.name: bride from Nadabath
people.description: Daughter of a great noble of Canaan brought from Nadabath to marry among the sons of Jambri; her wedding procession was ambushed by Jonathan and Simon.

people.name: bridegroom of the sons of Jambri
people.description: Bridegroom who came out with his friends to meet the bridal procession and was attacked in the ambush avenging John.

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch cited as found faithful in temptation; ancestor claimed by Spartans and Jews.

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Patriarch who kept the commandment and became lord of Egypt.

people.name: Phinehas
people.description: Priest whose zeal against Zimri is the model for Mattathias.

people.name: Zimri
people.description: Simeonite son of Salu killed by Phinehas.

people.name: Salu
people.description: Father of Zimri.

people.name: Joshua
people.description: Became a judge in Israel.

people.name: Caleb
people.description: Received an inheritance for his testimony.

people.name: David
people.description: King praised for mercy and for defeating the Philistine giant.
people.identity_note: 'City of David' (1:33; 2:31; 7:32; 14:36) is a place name and is not counted.

people.name: Elijah
people.description: Prophet taken up into heaven for zeal.

people.name: Hananiah
people.description: Companion of Daniel saved from the flame.

people.name: Azariah
people.description: Companion of Daniel saved from the flame.

people.name: Mishael
people.description: Companion of Daniel saved from the flame.

people.name: Daniel
people.description: Delivered from the lions.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.description: Pharaoh who pursued Israel to the Red Sea.

people.name: the mighty warrior (Goliath)
people.description: Philistine champion defeated by David, alluded to in Judas' prayer.

people.name: Saul
people.description: Father of Jonathan.

people.name: Jonathan son of Saul
people.description: Delivered the Philistine army into Israel's hands with his armor bearer.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Jonathan Apphus and Jonathan son of Absalom.

people.name: Jonathan's armor bearer
people.description: Armor bearer of Jonathan son of Saul.

people.name: Aaron
people.description: Ancestor of the priest Alcimus ('of the seed of Aaron').

people.name: Joarib
people.description: Priestly ancestor/course from which Mattathias' family descended.
people.identity_note: Joarib = Jehoiarib, head of the first priestly course (1 Chr 24:7); used here as ancestral house name.

people.name: king whose envoys blasphemed (Sennacherib)
people.description: Assyrian king whose army was struck by the angel (185,000), alluded to in Judas' prayer.
people.identity_note: Not named in the verse; the 185,000 figure identifies 2 Kings 19:35.

dated_events.event: Antiochus Epiphanes begins to reign
Antiochus returns from Egypt and plunders the Jerusalem temple
Abomination of desolation set up on the altar
First pagan sacrifice on the idol altar
dated_events.note: Text gives only 'the twenty-fifth day of the month'; context implies Chislev of year 145 (cf. 4:54). Year inferred from 1:54.

dated_events.event: Death and burial of Mattathias at Modin
Antiochus leaves Antioch for Persia, leaving Lysias in charge
Rededication of the altar and temple by Judas
Annual eight-day feast of dedication ordained
dated_events.note: Recurring festival from 25 Chislev; year not restated.

dated_events.event: Death of Antiochus Epiphanes in Persia
Judas besieges the Jerusalem citadel
Demetrius son of Seleucus comes from Rome and begins to reign
Battle of Adasa; Nicanor killed
dated_events.note: Year not stated in the text; month number 12 = Adar (conventional).

dated_events.event: Annual Nicanor's Day ordained
Bacchides and Alcimus encamp against Jerusalem
Alcimus orders the inner court wall pulled down and is stricken
Alexander Epiphanes seizes Ptolemais and reigns
Jonathan puts on the high-priestly garments at the feast of tabernacles
Ptolemy brings Cleopatra to Ptolemais; wedding to Alexander
Demetrius son of Demetrius comes from Crete
Demetrius II becomes king
The yoke of the Gentiles removed from Israel
Contracts dated 'first year of Simon, the great high priest'
dated_events.note: Regnal year 1 of Simon = Seleucid year 170 (13:41).

dated_events.event: Simon enters the Jerusalem citadel
Demetrius II goes to Media and is captured by Arsaces
Decree honouring Simon proclaimed at Asaramel
dated_events.note: Also 'the third year of Simon the high priest'; month number 6 = Elul (conventional).

dated_events.event: Antiochus VII enters his ancestral land; Trypho deserted
Simon goes down to Jericho, where he and his sons are murdered

excluded_names.Jacob: used of the nation ('house/race of Jacob'), not the patriarch as an individual
excluded_names.Esau: used of the Edomites ('children of Esau')
excluded_names.Jambri: clan name ('children of Jambri'); no individual Jambri acts
excluded_names.Sampsames: place/state in the Roman circular list

notes: Seleucid-era years are as stated in the text (era begins 312/311 BC; 1 Maccabees' Judean reckoning is often taken from spring 311 BC). Namesakes separated: Antiochus x6 (III, IV Epiphanes, V Eupator, VI, VII Sidetes, father of Numenius); Demetrius x2 (I Soter, II Nicator); Alexander x2 (the Great, Balas); Ptolemy x4 (VI Philometor incl. 1:18 and 10:51-11:18, VIII at 15:16, son of Dorymenes, son of Abubus); Philip x3 (II, V, friend of Antiochus IV); Apollonius x2 (Samaria 3:10, Coelesyria 10:69); John x4 (father of Mattathias, Gaddis, father of Eupolemus, Hyrcanus); Judas x3 (Maccabaeus, son of Chalphi, son of Simon); Jonathan x2 of this era (Apphus, son of Absalom) plus Jonathan son of Saul; Mattathias x3 (patriarch, son of Absalom, son of Simon); Simon x1 (Thassi) plus Simeon the grandfather; Joseph x2 (patriarch, son of Zacharias); Eleazar x2; Jason x2 (possibly the same, not merged); Azariah x2 (Daniel's companion, Azarias the commander); only one Timothy in this book. Nicanor of 3:38 and of ch.7 merged (usual identification). Ptolemy VI of 1:18 merged with the king of 10:51-11:18 on historical grounds. Unnamed groups not entered: Jonathan's two sons sent as hostages (13:16), Alexander's servants (1:6), the Roman 'general' (8:10), messengers (6:5; 16:21), the noble father of the bride (9:37). 'The king' is used without a name in many verses; refs list named verses plus clear pronoun/title references only where identification is certain. Parent/spouse objects carry ref_id in addition to ref_name because names repeat. dated_events month numbers follow the text where given (4:52 ninth month = Chislev; 16:14 eleventh month = Sebat) and conventional numbering otherwise (Adar 12, Elul 6); month_name records the text's month name. Death verses: Alexander 1:7, apostate and officer at Modin 2:24-25, Mattathias 2:70, Apollonius 3:11, Eleazar 6:46, Antiochus IV 6:16, Antiochus V & Lysias 7:4, Nicanor 7:43, Judas 9:18, John Gaddis 9:36 (implied), Alcimus 9:56, Demetrius I 10:50, Alexander Balas 11:17, Ptolemy VI 11:18, Jonathan 13:23, Antiochus VI 13:31, Simon and sons Mattathias and Judas 16:16.
